title: Extension Guidelines for Rice Stubble and Straw Burning Reduction Management of Farmers in Prachinburi Province / แนวทางการส่งเสริมการจัดการตอซังและฟางข้าวเพื่อลดการเผาของเกษตรกรผู้ปลูกข้าวในจังหวัดปราจีนบุรี
author: Siriwan Deeying; ศิริวรรณ ดียิ่ง; Jinda Khlibtong; จินดา ขลิบทอง; Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University; jinda.khl@stou.ac.th
category: การส่งเสริมและการผลิต
abstract: The objectives of this research were to study 1) general and rice production conditions of farmers 2) farmers’ knowledge of rice stubble and straw burning reduction management 3) farmers’ practices in managing rice stubble and straw to reduce open burning 4) problems and suggestions regarding rice stubble and straw burning reduction management of farmers 5) farmers’ access to and needs for extension services in rice stubble and straw burning reduction management and 6) extension guidelines for rice stubble and straw burning reduction management of farmers This research was a survey research. The population in this study was 22,108 rice production farmers in Prachinburi Province who had registered with the Department of Agricultural Extension in 2024/25. The sample size of 204 people was determined using Taro Yamane’s formula with a margin of error of 0.07. The sample group was classified into 102 rice farmers participating in the Project of Extension for Stop Burning at Agricultural Area and 102 general rice farmers through stratified sampling method. Data were collected using an interview form and were analyzed using descriptive statistics such as frequency distribution, percentage, minimum value, maximum value, mean, standard deviation, ranking, content analysis, t-test and multiple regression analysis. The results of the research found that 1) most of farmers in both groups were female. Farmers participating in the project had an average age of 60.70 years old, an average of 1.70 household agricultural laborers, and an average rice cultivation area of 24.65 rai, while general farmers had an average age of 57.20 years old, 1.91 household agricultural laborers, and an average cultivation area of 29.16 rai. The factors that had a statistically significant affected on farmers’ rice stubble and straw burning at the 0.05 level included the size of the rice cultivation area, the type of rice cultivation, the number of agricultural laborers in the household and land rental for rice cultivation. 2) The two groups of farmers differed significantly in their knowledge of rice stubble and straw management at the 0.05 level in almost all subtopics except for incorporation of rice stubble and straw and the utilization of microorganisms for rice stubble and straw decomposition. 3) Farmers in the project group had a lower average level of practice in rice stubble and straw management than general farmers. Both groups engaged highly in baled rice straw collection, while general farmers practiced incorporation of rice stubble and straw at a higher level. 4) The main problem for both groups was the utilization of rice stubble and straw for renewable energy or biochar. A key suggestion for rice stubble and straw burning reduction management is the needs for government support in providing agricultural machinery and agricultural inputs for rice stubble and straw management. 5) Farmers expressed the highest needs for rice stubble and straw management extension in the forms of training and knowledge transfer sessions, demonstrations, field demonstration and continuous follow-up visits from agricultural extensionist, and 6) extension guidelines for rice stubble and straw burning reduction management include time-specific management practices through collaborative mechanisms among relevant public and private sectors, linking rice straw markets with buyers, conducting training and knowledge transfer activities with field demonstration, and continuous follow-up visits from agricultural extensionist. บทที่ 2
